items.title: fix(mime): add .mjs and .cjs to COMMON_MIME_TYPES
items.body:
`.mjs` (ES module) and `.cjs` (CommonJS module) files are absent from `COMMON_MIME_TYPES`. When `serveStatic` serves a `.mjs` file, `getType` returns `undefined` and no `Content-Type` header is set.

Browsers enforce strict MIME checking for `<script type="module">` — a missing content-type causes a network error and the module fails to load entirely.

The fix adds both extensions mapped to `"text/javascript"`, consistent with `.js` and with [RFC 9239](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9239).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * `.mjs` and `.cjs` files are now identified as JavaScript files.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: fix(cookie): size cookie chunks by their encoded length
items.body:
## Summary

`setChunkedCookie` splits the raw value every `chunkMaxLength` (default 4000) characters. Each chunk is then percent-encoded by `setCookie` (`encodeURIComponent` by default), and that encoding makes it longer: `"`, `{`, `:`, `,` and spaces become 3 bytes, and non-ASCII characters become 6–12 bytes. So the stored chunks can be far larger than the ~4KB the chunking is meant to stay under.

```ts
setChunkedCookie(event, "cart", JSON.stringify(cart)); // 7501 characters
// Set-Cookie: cart=__chunked__2
// Set-Cookie: cart.1=… (9195 bytes)
// Set-Cookie: cart.2=… (7932 bytes)
```

Browsers drop cookies over 4096 bytes, so the chunks never come back. On the next request `getChunkedCookie` sees `__chunked__2` with the chunks missing and returns `undefined`. The data is lost without any error.

A second failure in the same slicing: `value.slice()` cuts at UTF-16 indexes, so a chunk boundary can split a surrogate pair (an emoji, for example). `encodeURIComponent` then throws `URIError: URI malformed`, and the handler fails with a 500.

Session cookies aren't affected: the sealed value is URL-safe ASCII. It hits apps that put JSON or user text into chunked cookies.

## Fix

A new internal helper, `splitCookieValue`, splits the value on code point boundaries, so a surrogate pair is never split. Each chunk is the longest run whose encoded form, using the same `encode` as `setCookie` (`options.encode` or `encodeURIComponent`), fits in `chunkMaxLength`. The helper measures whole candidate chunks (gallop, then bisect), so custom encoders like base64 whose length isn't additive per character are sized correctly too. A code point that can't fit even alone throws before any header is written. For values that don't grow when encoded (such as sealed sessions), the chunks are exactly the same as before, so all existing chunk snapshots are unchanged. The chunk-count cap still applies, and the helper stops as soon as it's exceeded.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests in `test/cookies.test.ts` (web and node, both setups):
  - `keeps every encoded chunk within chunkMaxLength and readable`: a 2771-character JSON value (7453 bytes encoded). Every `Set-Cookie` value is ≤ 4000 bytes, and `getChunkedCookie` reads back the original.
  - `does not split a surrogate pair across chunks`: `"12345678901😀abc"` with `chunkMaxLength: 12` round-trips.
  - `sizes chunks for a custom encoder by the whole encoded chunk`: a `btoa` encoder with budget 40 gives 4 chunks of 30 characters, which round-trip.
  - `throws when a single character cannot fit in chunkMaxLength`
  - on `main` (62c2632): 16 failures (`expected 7453 to be less than or equal to 4000`, `URIError: URI malformed` → 500, …)
  - with this change: `test/cookies.test.ts` and `test/session.test.ts` 192/192
- [x] Full `vitest run` (node 24): 2872 passed, 66 skipped
- [x] `oxlint .`, `oxfmt --check .`, `tsc --noEmit`, `obuild` and `git diff --check` are clean

This bug was found and fixed by an AI agent (breken-ai) and verified with the red/green tests above.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Chunked cookies now respect size limits based on their encoded representation, including when values contain multibyte characters.
  * Character pairs remain intact across chunks, and chunk sizes account for the complete output of custom encoders.
  * If a single character cannot fit within the encoded size limit, the operation returns an HTTP 500 error without writing response headers.
  * The existing 100-chunk limit remains in place.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

issue.title: rules: skip `redirect` when the request is already at the target (avoid `false` resets)
issue.body:
When a `redirect` rule's target falls inside its own pattern, requests to the target redirect again. Today the only fix is a `false` reset, which is easy to forget and hard to get right:

```ts
routeRules({
  "/docs/**": { redirect: "/docs/v2/**" },
});
// GET /docs/intro    → 307 /docs/v2/intro
// GET /docs/v2/intro → 307 /docs/v2/v2/intro  (and so on)
```

The same happens with the new request conditions (#1557) when redirecting Markdown requests to `.md` files:

```ts
{
  "GET:MD /blog/**": { redirect: "/blog/**.md" },
  // Required today, and only covers one segment (`/blog/a/b.md` still loops):
  "GET:MD /blog/*.md": { redirect: false },
}
```

### Proposal

A `redirect` rule never fires when the request path already has the shape of its target, meaning the request is already at a URL this rule could have sent it to.

- `to: "/blog/**.md"`: skip when the path starts with `/blog/` and ends with `.md`, at any depth.
- `to: "/docs/v2/**"`: skip when the path starts with `/docs/v2/`.
- `to: "/new"` (no `**`): skip only an exact redirect to the current path.
- Targets on another origin keep today's behavior. Only the path part of `to` is compared, not the query or fragment.

The earlier example then works without a reset:

```ts
{ "GET:MD /blog/**": { redirect: "/blog/**.md" } }
```

The prefix and suffix around `**` can be worked out at startup. Each request then costs one `startsWith`/`endsWith` check, and only when a redirect rule matches.

### Trade-off

This changes current behavior. A rule that deliberately redirects `/a/b/c` to `/a/b/b/c` would stop firing. That seems unlikely to be intended, but it should go in the changelog. `proxy` could get the same guard, but it doesn't loop on the client side, so it can wait.

### Alternatives considered

- **Path checks in conditions** (`MD: { headers, path: /(?<!\.md)$/ }`): more general, but you'd need a negative regex to say "doesn't end in `.md`".
- **Exclusion syntax in patterns** (`/blog/**` except `*.md`): rou3 has no negation, so this needs new pattern syntax.

items.title: getValidatedQuery should account for ambiguous data
items.body:
### Describe the feature

## Premise

readQuery() as it is currently only works if you either

1. have extremely simple data - basically exclusively strings.
2. make a custom schema with coercing (assuming the validation library supports everything needed) for every API endpoint, not really being able to reuse existing schemas
3. send all data as body payload (this wouldn't be a problem if GET and DELETE were allowed to have bodies)
4. send all data as stringified JSON
5. or (like me) make a shim that tries its best at adjusting the data to better fit a schema

none of these options are particularly enticing, so (imo) there should be a system to somehow fix this in h3.

## My shim/workaround

without posting code, I basically crawl through the zod type definition alongside the passed data and adjust the data where it can't be unambiguously represented by query parameters.

I'm not sure how viable this is for h3 considering it's supposed to be somewhat validator-agnostic… But then again, having this feature for a limited amount of libraries would be better than having it for none at all.

## Additional notes

zod has already declined to implement a version of this on their side: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/2873

### Additional information

- [ ] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?

items.title: Idiomatic way to create a reusable auth middleware that supports both app.use() and per-route handler wrapping in H3 v2
items.body:
I'm building a reusable middleware library with H3 v2 and want to support two usage patterns from a single function:

```ts
// Pattern A: app-wide via app.use()
app.use(withAuth({ role: 'user' }))

// Pattern B: per-route handler wrapping (e.g. Nitro/Nuxt file routes)
export default withAuth({ role: 'user' }, async (event) => {
  return event.context.authCtx
})
```

My current implementation returns `defineMiddleware(...)` for pattern A and `defineEventHandler({ middleware: [m], handler })` for pattern B.

Two questions:

1. For pattern B, is `defineEventHandler({ middleware, handler })` the right approach, or is there a more idiomatic way to compose a pre-handler middleware with a route handler?

2. For Nuxt's `server/middleware/` files, the convention is `export default defineEventHandler(...)` but pattern A returns a `Middleware` type. Is it safe/correct to export a `Middleware` directly from a Nitro server middleware file, or should it always be wrapped in `defineEventHandler`?

Thanks!

items.title: Shorthand for throwing HTTP errors
items.body:
Hi, not sure if this has been discussed before, but wanted to share an idea.

Right now when I want to return a 404 from a handler I write:

```ts
throw createError({ statusCode: 404 })
```

It would be nice if h3 accepted a simpler shorthand like:

```ts
throw 404
```

Basically: let the thrown value map to an HTTP error directly, without the `createError({ statusCode: ... })` wrapper.

`createError` / `new HTTPError({ ... })` would still be there for the richer cases (custom `data`, headers, message, etc.).

PR: #1372

## Custom strings

We could also tried supporting a string form to carry a message:

```ts
throw "404 Lesson not found"
```

But parsing the status out of the string needs a regex and bumps the bundle size a bit, so I left it out of the PR. For messages, sticking with `new HTTPError({ status: 404, message: "Lesson not found" })` feels cleaner.

items.body:
Hi. I suggest 3 approaches to try:

## 1. Config

We can try to add `import 'newrelic'` to the top of `nuxt.config.js`? This should partially work as this is almost the topmost entry-point. 

## 2. CLI Wrapper

We may create a custom cli wrapper in the root of the project:

`~/nuxt.js`:

```js
require('newrelic')
require('nuxt/bin/nuxt')
````

And then inside `package.json`:

```diff
scripts: {
-- "start": "nuxt start",
++ "start": "node ./nuxt start",
}
```

## 3. Module (best)

If newrelic is similar to sentry, this is not **required** to be the first import, we can do this via a nuxt module and it globally should register itself to the entire process:

`modules/newrelic.js`

```js
export default async function() {
  await import('newrelic')
}
```

`nuxt.config.js`

```js
export default {
    modules: [
        '~/modules/newrelic'
    ]
}
```

items.title: fix(validate): preserve repeated query values in defineValidatedHandler
items.body:
## Summary

- `defineValidatedHandler` built its query validation input with `Object.fromEntries(url.searchParams.entries())`, which keeps only the **last** value for repeated keys (`?tag=a&tag=b` → `{ tag: "b" }`).
- Feed validators through the existing `parseQuery` helper (same shape as `getQuery`) and write array results back as repeated `URLSearchParams` entries.

## Reproduction

```ts
defineValidatedHandler({
  validate: { query: z.object({ tag: z.array(z.string()) }) },
  handler: (event) => event.url.searchParams.getAll("tag"),
});
// GET /?tag=a&tag=b
// before: validation fails / sees only "b"
// after: validator input `{ tag: ["a", "b"] }`, handler returns `["a", "b"]`
```

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run test/handler.test.ts` (23 passed)
- [ ] CI

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Repeated query parameters are now preserved when validated, so handlers can receive and return all values instead of only the last one.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: fix(cookie): size cookie chunks by their encoded length
items.body:
## Summary

`setChunkedCookie` splits the raw value every `chunkMaxLength` (default 4000) characters. Each chunk is then percent-encoded by `setCookie` (`encodeURIComponent` by default), and that encoding makes it longer: `"`, `{`, `:`, `,` and spaces become 3 bytes, and non-ASCII characters become 6–12 bytes. So the stored chunks can be far larger than the ~4KB the chunking is meant to stay under.

```ts
setChunkedCookie(event, "cart", JSON.stringify(cart)); // 7501 characters
// Set-Cookie: cart=__chunked__2
// Set-Cookie: cart.1=… (9195 bytes)
// Set-Cookie: cart.2=… (7932 bytes)
```

Browsers drop cookies over 4096 bytes, so the chunks never come back. On the next request `getChunkedCookie` sees `__chunked__2` with the chunks missing and returns `undefined`. The data is lost without any error.

A second failure in the same slicing: `value.slice()` cuts at UTF-16 indexes, so a chunk boundary can split a surrogate pair (an emoji, for example). `encodeURIComponent` then throws `URIError: URI malformed`, and the handler fails with a 500.

Session cookies aren't affected: the sealed value is URL-safe ASCII. It hits apps that put JSON or user text into chunked cookies.

## Fix

A new internal helper, `splitCookieValue`, splits the value on code point boundaries, so a surrogate pair is never split. Each chunk is the longest run whose encoded form, using the same `encode` as `setCookie` (`options.encode` or `encodeURIComponent`), fits in `chunkMaxLength`. The helper measures whole candidate chunks (gallop, then bisect), so custom encoders like base64 whose length isn't additive per character are sized correctly too. A code point that can't fit even alone throws before any header is written. For values that don't grow when encoded (such as sealed sessions), the chunks are exactly the same as before, so all existing chunk snapshots are unchanged. The chunk-count cap still applies, and the helper stops as soon as it's exceeded.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests in `test/cookies.test.ts` (web and node, both setups):
  - `keeps every encoded chunk within chunkMaxLength and readable`: a 2771-character JSON value (7453 bytes encoded). Every `Set-Cookie` value is ≤ 4000 bytes, and `getChunkedCookie` reads back the original.
  - `does not split a surrogate pair across chunks`: `"12345678901😀abc"` with `chunkMaxLength: 12` round-trips.
  - `sizes chunks for a custom encoder by the whole encoded chunk`: a `btoa` encoder with budget 40 gives 4 chunks of 30 characters, which round-trip.
  - `throws when a single character cannot fit in chunkMaxLength`
  - on `main` (62c2632): 16 failures (`expected 7453 to be less than or equal to 4000`, `URIError: URI malformed` → 500, …)
  - with this change: `test/cookies.test.ts` and `test/session.test.ts` 192/192
- [x] Full `vitest run` (node 24): 2872 passed, 66 skipped
- [x] `oxlint .`, `oxfmt --check .`, `tsc --noEmit`, `obuild` and `git diff --check` are clean

This bug was found and fixed by an AI agent (breken-ai) and verified with the red/green tests above.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Chunked cookies now respect size limits based on their encoded representation, including when values contain multibyte characters.
  * Character pairs remain intact across chunks, and chunk sizes account for the complete output of custom encoders.
  * If a single character cannot fit within the encoded size limit, the operation returns an HTTP 500 error without writing response headers.
  * The existing 100-chunk limit remains in place.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: fix(mime): add .mjs and .cjs to COMMON_MIME_TYPES
items.body:
`.mjs` (ES module) and `.cjs` (CommonJS module) files are absent from `COMMON_MIME_TYPES`. When `serveStatic` serves a `.mjs` file, `getType` returns `undefined` and no `Content-Type` header is set.

Browsers enforce strict MIME checking for `<script type="module">` — a missing content-type causes a network error and the module fails to load entirely.

The fix adds both extensions mapped to `"text/javascript"`, consistent with `.js` and with [RFC 9239](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9239).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * `.mjs` and `.cjs` files are now identified as JavaScript files.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
